diagnosis_explanation: You have a urinary tract infection. This means there is an infection in your bladder or kidneys. You may have had a fever because of this infection. Your doctor has prescribed medicine to treat the infection.
medication_rationale:
Enteric-coated aspirin 81 mg:
This medicine is new for you. It can help prevent blood clots.
This may lower your risk of heart problems.
You might get some stomach upset. This is usually mild.
Call your doctor if you see blood in your urine or stool.
Also call if you have black or tarry stools.

TriCor 48 mg:
This medicine helps lower your body's cholesterol.
Cholesterol is a type of fat in your blood.
High cholesterol can lead to heart problems.
You may notice mild nausea or stomach pain.
Call your doctor if you get muscle aches or weakness.
Also call if your skin or eyes look yellow.

Zantac 40 mg:
This medicine reduces the acid in your stomach.
It can help with heartburn or an upset stomach.
You might feel mild nausea or get headaches.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
Also call if your heart beats very fast.

Lisinopril 20 mg:
This medicine helps your blood pressure get lower.
Lower blood pressure protects your heart and kidneys.
You might get a dry cough. This is common.
Call your doctor if your face or lips swell.
Also call if you feel dizzy often.

Mobic 75 mg:
This medicine helps with arthritis pain.
It reduces swelling and eases joint stiffness.
You may notice stomach upset or feel tired.
Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain.
Also call if you see dark urine or blood.
Important: Do not stop taking this medicine without calling your doctor first.

Metformin 500 mg:
This medicine helps control your blood sugar.
It is used if you have diabetes.
You might feel nausea or have diarrhea.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
Also call if you feel very weak or tired.

Macrodantin:
This medicine fights the germs causing your infection.
It helps clear up your urinary tract infection.
You may have an upset stomach or feel dizzy.
Call your doctor if you get a rash or fever.
Also call if your urine turns brown.

Zocor 20 mg:
This medicine lowers the cholesterol in your blood.
It helps protect your heart from future problems.
You might get mild stomach upset or constipation.
Call your doctor if you have muscle pain.
Also call if your skin or eyes look yellow.

Effexor XR 37.5 mg:
This medicine can help improve your mood.
It is used for depression and anxiety.
You may feel sleepy or have mild nausea.
Call your doctor if you have thoughts of harming yourself.
Also call if your heart beats very fast or skips.
Important: Do not stop taking this medicine without calling your doctor first.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired or sore after your procedures. This is normal.
- You can do light activities around your home.
- Continue your water exercise five days a week.
- Eat foods from the 1800-calorie ADA diet plan.
- Drink plenty of water to help clear the infection.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101°F.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worse pain.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes twice a day.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy levels should start to improve this week.
- You can return to most normal home activities.
- Keep up with water exercise five days a week.
- Follow the 1800-calorie ADA diet plan.
- Drink plenty of water each day.
- Watch for signs of infection like burning when you pee.
- Call your doctor if symptoms of infection return or worsen.
- Your goal this week is to increase your walking time to 15 minutes.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel stronger and have more energy.
- You can do more around the house.
- Continue water exercise five days a week.
- Stick to your 1800-calorie ADA diet.
- Ensure you are drinking enough water daily.
- You may feel mild discomfort from the lumbar puncture. This is okay.
- Call your doctor if you have a headache that does not get better.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 20 minutes each day.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel much closer to your normal self.
- You can gradually increase your activity levels.
- Keep up with water exercise five days a week.
- Continue following the 1800-calorie ADA diet.
- Stay well hydrated by drinking water.
- You may resume normal daily activities.
- Call your doctor if you have any concerns about your recovery.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 30 minutes each day.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel much better within 4 weeks.
- Continue drinking plenty of water.
- Keep following your 1800-calorie ADA diet.
- Listen to your body and do not overdo it.
- Urinary tract infections can take time to fully clear.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Cannot breathe or gasping for air: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain or pressure that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that will not stop: Apply firm pressure right away.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: Call 911 or have someone call.
- Seizure or losing control: Call 911 right away.
- Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, trouble speaking.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 degrees F: You may have a bad infection.
- Wound looks infected: red streaks, pus, or warm skin.
- Pain is severe and not helped by medicine: Seek care for bad pain.
- Cannot keep any fluids down: You may get too dry.
- Confusion or disorientation that is new: Get checked for urgent problems.
- Significant swelling in one leg: This could be a blood clot.
- Sudden weight gain of 2+ pounds in one day: Fluid may be building up.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly getting better: This is a good sign.
- Questions about your medicine or dose: Your doctor can help guide you.
- Mild redness at a wound site: This can happen while you heal.
- Mild swelling without pain: This may go away on its own.
- Feeling tired but it is improving: Rest can help your body heal.
- Nausea without any vomiting: Try small sips of clear fluids.
